A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–I. Their text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: Figure 1(b) reports an original descriptive analysis of the surveyed literature: 6 publications and 1 preprint for 2024, and 17 publications and 24 preprints for 2025. This bibliometric analysis qualifies, although Table 4 compiles experimental results attributed to other studies.

after.justification: Figure 1(b) retains the survey's original publication/preprint counts for 2024–2025. The benchmark scores in Table 4 remain attributed compilations rather than newly conducted model experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendices C, G–I retain the same retrieval formulations, training objectives and descriptions of existing methods. No proposed algorithm or component is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: The dataset and task coverage in Section 4, Appendix A and Tables 3 and 6 is unchanged. Neither version introduces additional training or evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 4 preserves the same methods within every retrieval and generation comparison block. The new Appendix D citations do not become additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported metrics and evaluation settings in Table 4 and Appendix B are unchanged. No data splits, model configurations, budgets or testing procedures are added or revised.

E4.justification: No ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests or empirical case studies are added or removed. Appendix E retains its existing literature-based discussion of failure modes and trade-offs.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or changes repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimation. The descriptive counts and compiled point estimates retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 1(b), the benchmark tables and appendix summaries retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 4 keeps RegionRAG's DocVQA R@10 at 99.4 and SimpleDoc's MMLongBench-Doc G-Acc at 60.58.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(25), covering retrieval, evaluation metrics and the ColBERT-style loss, remain unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same survey contributions: connecting multimodal RAG with document understanding, organizing methods by taxonomy, compiling benchmarks and outlining challenges. The novelty claim and scientific scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning OCR, granular representations, benchmark validity, security and deployment costs remain unchanged. Appendix D adds citations to existing arguments without introducing new explanations or qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page URL identifying the survey's project repository; v2 only promises an open repository in Limitations. This improves access information without establishing changes to implementation or experimental settings.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds six references: IDEAL and CRIS in the granular-representation discussion, and Gao et al. (2024), Jia et al. (2025a,b) and Xiang et al. (2026) in the security discussion. The survey's broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations and internship wording, adds funding acknowledgments and makes small citation and hyphenation edits. The substantive prose and section/appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 standardizes citations to abbreviated year forms, changing column widths and scaling. Figure 2 moves from page 3 to page 5, Table 3 moves from page 7 to page 8, and first-page notes become footnotes. Graphics, table contents and captions otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a concrete project-repository pointer absent from v2, adds funding disclosure and makes Table 2's citation formatting more consistent. These offer modest gains in documentation and usability. The survey's substantive synthesis, mathematical exposition, results and limitations remain unchanged.
